description.text:
Adds light globally to the diffuse (albedo) surface response for surface shaders which respect this shading global.
Setting ambient to 1.0 in a scene with no lights makes surfaces emit their diffuse color as if illuminated equally from all directions with an implied light with intensity 1.0 (result will look flatly illuminated.)

Math to use when merging multiple surface samples in depth:
  • premult-blend - Premult A then Under(B + A*Aa*(1-Ba)) or Over(B*(1-Aa) + A*Aa) - best for data Aovs
  • blend - Under(B + A*(1-Ba)) or Over(B*(1-Aa) + A) - best for color Aovs
  • plus - B + A
  • min - min(B, A) - best for Z
  • mid - (B + A)/2
  • max - max(B, A)

Source of Aov from shading results. A list of shading variable layers extended if geometry prims provide primvars. For example if a geometry mesh object provides a primvar named 'myUV' then it will appear at the end of this list along with its size (float, vec2, vec3, vec4.) Predefined shading attributes:
  • Cf - Geometry color (from primvar if available)
  • Co - Geometry opacity (from primvar if available)
  • presence - Surface presence (physical solidity)
  • Oi - Surface rgb opacity (optical transparency)
  • Zlinear - Linear-projected distance (classic Z)
  • Zdistance - Camera ray distance
    • -------------------
  • Ps - Shading position
  • Pg - Geometric position
  • Ns - Shading normal
  • Ng - Geometric normal
  • Ts - Shading tangent
  • UV - Surface parametric-uv coordinate (from primvar if available)
  • UVW - Surface parametric-w (Z for volumes, from primvar if available)
  • St - Texture coordinate (different than parametric-UV if modified by shader)
  • MotionFwd - Forward motion-vectors
  • MotionBwd - Backwards motion-vectors
    • -------------------
  • albedo - Surface albedo reflectance color
  • diffuse - Surface diffuse scatter lobe contribution
  • specular - Surface specular lobe contribution
  • transmission - Surface transmission lobe contribution
  • emission - Surface emission contribution
  • shadow - Surface shadow transmission color

@b;Camera/Projection

Camera ray far clipping distance. Camera rays will not intersect anything further than this distance.
Note - this is the -radial- clipping distance from the camera's origin, -not- a clipping plane. A plane is like a straight wall in front of the camera while radial clipping is measured as the direct distance from the camera's location to an object.

Camera ray near clipping distance. Camera rays will not intersect anything closer than this distance.
Note - this is the -radial- clipping distance from the camera's origin, -not- a clipping plane. A plane is like a straight wall in front of the camera while radial clipping is measured as the direct distance from the camera's location to an object.

Set the per-pixel sampling count for camera rays.

The total number of samples is the sampling grid size squared, or gridsize*gridsize. Increasing this will smooth out motionblur noise and aliasing at the cost of increased computation and a reduction in speed.

Sampling grid locations are stratified such that each location is randomly placed within each grid box and distributed so there is only one sample falling in each.

When camera samples mode is set to the 'custom' option this value determines the camera sample grid width/height size. A value of 4 means a 4x4 grid of 16 samples, while 13 is a 13x13 grid of 169 samples.
Value is clamped between 1 and 64 before use (1..4096 total samples per pixel)

When copying data aovs from shaded surfaces, copy from the nearest surface with the largest coverage. For example in a pixel with two surfaces being combined if the closest surface contributes only one sample to the output and the farther sample contributes four samples, pick the farther sample to output data aovs from since it is the 'dominant' surface in the pixel.

How to resolve material binding attributes at each renderable prim:
  • auto - choose the best binding attribute in order of importance: 'full' then `all purpose` ('preview' bindings are ignored and must be manually selected)
  • full - use only the 'full' binding attribute on the prim, if it exists
  • preview - use only the 'preview' binding attribute on the prim, if it exists
  • all purpose - use only the `all purpose` binding attribute on the prim, if it exists
  • off - do not use any of the binding attributes on the prim, disabling the material

List of material family names that the renderer will attempt to use for material connections, in search order priority.
Default is 'slr mtlx' where 'slr' is the native material family for ScanlineRender and 'mtlx' is the MaterialX material family. If a material provides multiple output connections then they are matched in the order of the family list (ie 'slr' first, then 'mtlx'.) If no match is made then the material binding fails and the default material (vert/face color) will be assigned.

  • Off - do not create any motion vectors
  • Distance - stores positional velocity between shutter open and close in the motion vector channel
  • Velocity - stores total positional velocity in the motion vector channel

Objects

ON: Output classic-style Nuke Z which is 1/Z-distance. 'No Object' is black 0.0 and the Z value -decreases- the further from camera. This is convenient to use in a compositor because it looks and acts much like a color channel and can be directly viewed. It will also pass through a filter without creating illegal 'nan' floating-point values. Note that 1/Z is NOT normalized Z. 1/Z is easily converted back to absoluteZ-distance by using another 1/Z. Normalizing involves scaling the Z by some near/far range and thus destroys the scene-space scale of the distance value. OFF: Output absolute Z-distance where 'No Object' = inf and the Z value -increases- the further from the camera. This is the world-space distance from the camera to the object. Note that the presence of floating point infinity can cause filters to create 'nan' outputs.
The number of pixels to render beyond the left/right and top/bottom of frame, if requested by subsequent operations.

Enable this to perspective-correct the Z-depth input from the background input, which will produce more accurate Z intersections, especially near camera.

Note - this is only required when the input image is from a perspective camera render and the Z depth channel contains linearly-projected Z depth. Other camera projections like spherical or cylindrical produce distance-from-camera Z depth which is the direct vector distance from the camera's origin to the shaded surface point.

Filter input scene prims by their 'purpose' attribute. Standard values for this are default, render, proxy, and guide. all disables purpose filtering so everything renders, and if none are enabled then nothing will be rendered.

Preset projection modes:
  • Render Camera - Take the projection mode from the camera.
  • Perspective - Objects in front of the camera have the illusion of depth defined by the camera's focal-length and aperture.
  • Orthographic - Objects are viewed using a parallel projection.
  • Spherical Map - The entire 360deg world is rendered as a spherical map.
  • Cylindrical - 360deg world horizontally cylindrically projected around camera.
  • UV Unwrap - The first or selected object renders its UV space into the output format. Use this to cook out texture maps.
Additionally loaded projection plugins come after the presets.

Diffuse ray max depth.
Diffuse rays will stop when this depth count is reached. The depth is incremented when a surface is shaded.

The maximum depth rays can 'bounce' to.
Ray max depth is tested and incremented for all ray types, so the max depth can be a mix of ray types.  For example, if the max depth is 4 then a ray bounce sequence like:
 ray#  type
 1     camera
 2     glossy
 3     glossy
 4     diffuse
 5     refraction
will stop at the 'diffuse' ray bounce which is ray #4 in the sequence.
However, if glossy max depth was set to only 1 then shading would stop at ray #2 terminating the sequence.
@b;Ray Options

Glossy ray max depth.
Glossy rays will stop when this depth count is reached. The depth is incremented when a surface is shaded.

Refraction ray max depth.
Refraction rays will stop when this depth count is reached. The depth is incremented when a surface is shaded.
Output only the render against black (zeros), don't overlay on background input.

When the bg input has a larger pixel bbox than its format size how should the renderer handle the extended bbox area outside the format's size. (note that any overscan expansion will still be taken into account for each of these modes):
  • Format - render region is the format size, and any extended bbox pixels are passed through unchanged.
  • Format Extend - render region is the format size, and automatically expanded to fill any extended bbox area.
  • Format Clip - render region is the format size, and the output bbox is clipped to the format.

Reverse the shading order from farthest surface to nearest surface.
The resulting greatest-coverage Z value will be from the farthest surface, however if the Aov Z merge mode is left at the 'min' default then you may get the smallest-coverage surface, so try changing it to 'max'

Shifts the frame time of input geometry, lights & cameras while keeping the renderer at the same output frame. For example if renderer is at frame 10 and offset is set to -1.0 then the objects, lights and cameras are sampled at frame 9.
The shift time can be in subframe amounts like -0.5 or 0.23 (see Note 2 below)

Note 1 - the noise sampling pattern seed is based on the -output- frame, not input frame.
Note 2 - shifting by subframe amounts may cause the frame number rounding on geometry and texture sources to pick unexpected frames, especially if the shutter open & close times straddle the integer frame 0 number (ex. shutter-open=-0.75 and shutter-close=+0.25
Output shadows into these channels

Shift the geometry intersection point to fake/simulate where the real surface would be.
Works best with moderately tessellated models, but may cause a 'scalloped' appearance along the shadow terminator in very low/coarse poly models. Turning this off will result in an alternative artifact which is entire polygons being shadowed despite appearing to be smoothly curved due to interpolated normal shading.
Enable shadowing cast from direct lighting.
This is how long the shutter should be open for when motion blurring. The value is in frames, so 0.5 is half a frame.

Biases samples toward shutter close or shutter open for stylized motion blur.
Negative values bias towards shutter open and positive values bias towards shutter close.

The number of 'time segments' used to interpolate motionblur.

A segment count of 0 effectively disables motionblur while a segment count of 1 creates a straight line blur. Increasing the number of segments beyond 1 subdivides the straight line into more time segments which is usually only necessary for heavy rotational blur - a spinning tire for example.

Note - if the camera or object motion is mostly linear increasing shutter segments should not produce any significant change in the motionblur's appearance.
Note 2 - with deforming geometry increasing shutter segments will only change the deforming object's blur if the deforming surface has additional time samples within the shutter range.

If the shutteroffset parameter is set to 'custom', this parameter is used to set the time that the shutter opens by adding it to the current frame.

Values are in frames, so -0.5 would open the shutter half a frame before the current frame.

The value of this controls how the shutter behaves with respect to the current frame value. It has four options
  • centred - centres the shutter around the frame, ie: open from f - shutter/2 to f + shutter/2
  • start - opens the shutter starting at the frame, ie: open from f to f + shutter
  • end - closes the shutter at the frame, ie: open from f - shutter to f
  • custom - opens the shutter at the time specified by the shuttercustomoffset parameter.

Global override - this takes precedence over per-prim settings.
Hint to renderer that the surface backface should be shaded like the front, ie a thin double-sided surface. The default behavior is to retrieve the sides info from the primitive 'doubleSided' attribute, if it exists.

This hint is important for the handling of normals on the surface backface especially when determining reflection/refraction angles.

Set to 'Double-Sided' if the surface is open like a card mesh and both front and back sides should be shaded
Set to 'Single-Sided' if the surface is closed like a cube or character mesh where only front faces should be shaded and backfaces are culled.

Global override - this takes precedence over per-prim settings.
Material is visible for front faces, back faces, or both sides. Note this is measuring the face's angle to the incoming ray direction, not the camera.
Affects all ray types.

When to enable the spatial (X/Y) jittering of the sampling screen location.
If this is 2 and camera samples >= 2 then spatial jitter will be applied to all samples.

When to enable random jittering in time. If this is 2 and camera samples >= 2 then time jitter will be applied to all samples.

description.text:
Scanline Render

'obj/scn' input: (required) Scene containing objects or an individual object to be rendered.

When connected to a Scene all the objects and lights connected to that scene will be rendered.

'cam' input: (optional) Viewing camera. If the camera input is not connected, the renderer will use a default camera positioned at the origin and facing in the negative Z direction.

'bg' input: (optional) Determines the output format and background. If not used, will default to root.format or root.proxy_format.

Deep Data Output
Scanline Render has the ability to output Deep data. It will only produce this data if there is a Deep node downstream.
